mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE above 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months by >1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month periods of INDPRO decline exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between rising FEDFUNDS and falling industrial production (INDPRO) over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with supply-side weakness, which amplifies recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while INDPRO falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% from the previous month, sustained for two months, signals a collapse in residential investment, which drags on construction-related equities and broader market sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls >10% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive months of >10% HOUST declines.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 0.4% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.4% for three consecutive months and acceleration present
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months of accelerating PAYEMS growth above 0.4%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates households are saving more and spending less, which typically precedes a demand slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises while GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises and GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters.
